title: Smooth purity for all admissible coefficients
statement:
Work in the standing separated finite-type $k$-scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], with the global purity datum of [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, and finite coefficient extensions inside the fixed $\Qlb$. Here admissible finite $A$ means any finite commutative ring killed by a power of $\ell$. The categories $\Dctf$ are the pro-etale condensed-module categories of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]; the twists are [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], with the finite-$A$ twist specified in [det-sp-finite-general-ring]. Integral categories are compared with completed, derived-complete categories by [sk-lem-integral-models], rational categories with scalar localizations by [det-sp-rational-localized-hom], and the $\Qlb$ category with finite condensed coefficient stages by [sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit]. These comparisons are equivalences, not identifications with discrete non-torsion constant-coefficient categories. Smoothness and relative dimension mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\Zl,\mathcal O_E,\Ql,E,\Qlb\}$ be any admissible coefficient
ring and let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth of pure relative dimension $d$. There is an
isomorphism of functors $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)\to\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$, given at
$K\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ by a canonical isomorphism in $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$

$$
\gamma_{f,\Lambda}(K):\ f_\Lambda^*K(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }f_\Lambda^!K.
$$

Here $f^!_\Lambda$ is the restriction of the right adjoint from
[sk-prop-sf-existence]. The isomorphism is compatible with change of
coefficients, base change and composition, with the normalization given by
integration on the affine line.

Moreover, $K\mapsto f_\Lambda^*K(d)[2d]$ is a right adjoint of
$Rf_{!,\Lambda}:\Dctf(X,\Lambda)\to\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$, with counit normalized by
integration on the affine line, and $\gamma_{f,\Lambda}$ is the *unique*
isomorphism of functors $f_\Lambda^*(-)(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}f_\Lambda^!$ on
$\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ compatible with the counits of the two adjunctions.

For étale $f$ we have $d=0$, and the theorem says $f_\Lambda^!\simeq f_\Lambda^*$
for every admissible $\Lambda$. For a smooth curve $C$ with structure map
$a:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ it gives
$a_{\Zl}^!\mathbf Z_{\ell,\operatorname{Spec}k}\simeq\mathbf Z_{\ell,C}(1)[2]$, a
single sheaf in degree $-2$.

proof.text: Put $F_{f,\Lambda}=Rf_{!,\Lambda}$ and $J_{f,\Lambda}=f^*_\Lambda(-)(d)[2d]$. We first construct an adjunction $F\dashv J$, with counit $t$, and then compare it to $F\dashv G$, where $G=f^!_\Lambda$ is the restriction in the statement. At finite coefficients the section-action/derived equivalence and the restriction of the localizing adjunction are precisely [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation]. At the other stages [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc] gives $\Dctf=\Dbc$, and [sk-thm-existence](2)--(4) supplies this restricted $F\dashv G$. Thus comparison of adjoints will take place on the same categories, not on the entire unbounded derived category.

source.place: Step 5: domains of the two adjunctions

proof.text: For finite $A$, choose $r\geq1$ with $\ell^r A=0$. Clause (3) of [det-sp-finite-general-ring] gives a natural isomorphism $\gamma^A:J_{f,A}\to G_{f,A}$, using the diagonal/DNC orientation; clauses (1)--(2) identify its normalization with scalar extension from $\mathbf Z/\ell^r$. Define $t^A_K=\varepsilon^A_K\circ F_{f,A}(\gamma^A_K)$. The Hom bijection for $G$, composed with the inverse of $\gamma^A$, gives $F_{f,A}\dashv J_{f,A}$ with counit $t^A$. The exponent independence in that node makes this independent of $r$. This covers arbitrary finite $A$, including nonregular rings, without assuming $\Dctf=\Dbc$ there.

source.place: Steps 1 and 5: finite purity and explicit adjunction

proof.text: The finite coefficient comparisons obey the actual equation $c_{A,B}(K)\circ(\gamma^A_K)_B=\gamma^B_{K_B}$ by [det-sp-reduction-compatibilities](3); its clause (2) gives transitivity for $A\to B\to C$. At $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ this includes [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity], which also transports orientations, traces and the composition/base-change squares. Finite geometric compatibility is supplied on general finite rings by [det-sp-composition-factors] and [det-sp-purity-bc-factors]. Hence the finite maps have all the required compatibilities before any limit is taken.

Fix $E$. By [sk-lem-integral-models](1)--(3), the integral condensed constructible category is the completed, derived-complete constructible category, and its pullback is the integral pullback used in the tower construction. Use the equivalence with normalized constructible towers in [det-sp-normalized-equivalence]. The normalized tower morphism $\gamma_{f,\bullet}$ exists and is natural by [det-sp-tower-gamma](2)--(3), not merely a compatible family in separate derived categories. The integral compact-support functor of the statement is the same functor as the realized tower functor by [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower](2). These facts identify both source and left adjoint, including their actions on morphisms.

source.place: Step 2: integral models and coherent realization

proof.text: Apply [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection]. It gives $F_{f,\mathcal O_E}\dashv H_f$, the realized tower counit $\varepsilon^H$, and a natural isomorphism $\gamma^H:J_{f,\mathcal O_E}\to H_f$ equal to $R\varprojlim\gamma_{f,\bullet}(\operatorname{red}K)$. Transfer the adjunction to $J$ by the Hom bijection and set $t_K=\varepsilon^H_K\circ F(\gamma^H_K)$. Its finite reductions are the finite counits and purity maps. This proves the integral explicit adjunction and an actual natural isomorphism; it does not infer uniqueness of a lift from equality of its individual reductions.

For the geometric compatibilities use the coherent reconstruction assertion [prop-pur-adic-reconstruction-trace-coherence]: the trace and the composition and smooth base-change equations reconstruct together with purity. To fix which integral family is meant, [lem-pur-tower-trace-purity-comparison] identifies the trace-transpose family with the actual tower family $\delta\circ\gamma^H$, where $\delta:H_f\to G_f$ is counit-preserving. Thus the reconstruction's coherent maps, rather than arbitrary lifts of their levels, are used here. For finite $E\subset F$, [det-sp-field-extension-towers](2) identifies coefficient change on these actual tower adjunctions, units, counits and purity maps, and asserts the coefficient-composition identity. These are the required integral compatibilities, including reduction to every uniformizer level.

For rational coefficients choose integral representatives $M_0,K_0$. The Hom comparison of [det-sp-rational-localized-hom], applied twice, carries the integral adjunction of Step 5 to
$$\operatorname{Hom}(F_E(M_0[1/\ell]),K_0[1/\ell])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_{\mathcal O_E}M_0,K_0)\otimes E\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M_0,J_{\mathcal O_E}K_0)\otimes E\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M_0[1/\ell],J_E(K_0[1/\ell])).$$
Its functor comparisons identify $F_E$ and pullback with the module-category operations in the statement; twists are the localized twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Every rational object has such a representative. Naturality extends from integral arrows to $h/\ell^s$ by $E$-linearity of the Hom bijections, so replacing representatives by an isomorphic one gives the same bijection. This proves $F_E\dashv J_E$, with counit the localized $t$. No claim that two arbitrarily chosen lattices are literally equal is used.

The rational purity is the scalar extension of integral purity by [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity], and its trace, composition and base-change coherence are [prop-pur-rational-purity-trace-coherence]. Its identification with the tower family used in Steps 5--7 is the last assertion of [lem-pur-tower-trace-purity-comparison]. The coefficient comparisons carry the rational adjunctions and their units and counits to those over $F$ by [sk-lem-sp-field-extension]; they compose for $E\subset F\subset L$. Consequently the preceding Hom bijections and counits commute with the finite-field transition maps. Taking $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ also gives the $\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $\mathbf Q_\ell$ cases.

source.place: Step 3: rational maps and coefficient coherence

proof.text:
For $\Qlb$, use the condensed finite-stage two-colimit of [sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit](2)--(4), together with the rational Hom equivalences of Step 7. The ambient compactification functor and pullback commute with extension from finite $E$: these are [det-prop-scalar-six-compact-support] for the listed maps $E\to\Qlb$ and [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback](1); twists have the coefficient comparisons in [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1). Choose $M_E,K_E$ over one finite field. Then
$$\operatorname{Hom}(F_{\Qlb}M,K)\cong\varinjlim_{F\supset E}\operatorname{Hom}(F_FM_F,K_F)\cong\varinjlim_{F\supset E}\operatorname{Hom}(M_F,J_FK_F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,J_{\Qlb}K).$$
The middle bijections commute with transition maps by Step 8. Objects, arrows and equalities descend to a common finite stage by the cited two-colimit theorem; hence the displayed bijection is natural and independent of presentations. It proves $F_{\Qlb}\dashv J_{\Qlb}$ with the finite-stage counit. In particular the common-stage construction is related to the condensed category by these equivalences, not equated to it by definition.

At every stage we now have $F\dashv J$ with its prescribed $t$, and $F\dashv G$ with $\varepsilon$ from Step 1. Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint], with its letters $G,J$ replaced by our $J,G$. It yields the natural isomorphism $\gamma:J\to G$ uniquely characterized by
$$\varepsilon_K\circ F(\gamma_K)=t_K.$$
This also shows that the comparisons already constructed at finite level and through the integral and rational stages are this same isomorphism: each is counit-preserving for exactly the adjunction just constructed. Thus both existence and uniqueness in the item refer to a fixed pair of adjunctions with fixed counits.

The finite, integral and rational composition/base-change identities of Steps 3, 6 and 8 persist at the $\Qlb$ stage: each equation is represented by the corresponding equation over a common finite coefficient field, where it is already proved. Their images are equal by functoriality of scalar extension and the Hom colimit. Changing the chosen exceptional adjoint does not change the coefficient equations: [det-sp-unique-adjoint-coefficients] identifies its coefficient mate by conjugation with the unique counit-preserving comparisons, and preserves their coefficient-composition equation. This gives the claimed compatibilities for the particular $f^!$ of [sk-prop-sf-existence], not just for an unnamed isomorphic functor.

source.place: Steps 3 and 5: compatibility for the chosen adjoint

proof.text: The normalization is fixed at finite level: [lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement] identifies the diagonal purity of the affine-line projection with the exceptional transpose of inverse projection formula followed by projective-line integration restricted to $\mathbf A^1$. At general finite $A$ the specified scalar construction in [det-sp-finite-general-ring](1)--(2) gives this same normalization. The tower counit has exactly these finite counits by [det-sp-tower-gluing](1),(3) and [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection]; rationalization and the finite-stage counit construction in Steps 7--9 preserve it. Hence $t$ is the normalized integration counit in every coefficient case, and Step 10 identifies it with $\varepsilon\circ F\gamma$.

Finally an etale $f$ is smooth of relative dimension zero, so its displayed twist and shift are $(0)[0]$, giving $f^!\simeq f^*$. For a smooth curve $a:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, evaluate $\gamma^{-1}$ at $\mathbf Z_\ell$ and use $a^*\mathbf Z_\ell=\mathbf Z_{\ell,C}$, the coefficient pullback of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1). The result is $a^!\mathbf Z_\ell\simeq\mathbf Z_{\ell,C}(1)[2]$. A degree-zero sheaf shifted by $[2]$ has its only cohomology in degree $-2$. The same substitution with dimension $d$ gives the dualizing-complex assertion of the source's Step 4.

source.place: Step 4 and the two specializations in the statement

All four faults of the earlier returns (NN a34be139, Q29 c11ba1dc, NI 77fb41c6) are repaired. (1) The counit t is pinned at every stage: finite t^A = ε∘F(γ^A) from det-sp-finite-general-ring(3); integral t = ε^H∘F(γ^H) from det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection; rational and Qlb t are the localized and finite-stage counits. (2) One integral family is used: γ^T = δ∘R lim γ_•, identified with the trace-transpose/reconstruction family by lem-pur-tower-trace-purity-comparison, whose last clause also gives γ^rat = Q_E(γ^T) for thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity and prop-pur-rational-purity-trace-coherence. (3) The Qlb categories are identified by sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit(2)-(4); E→Qlb is a listed map for det-prop-scalar-six-compact-support. (4) Arbitrary finite A uses det-sp-finite-general-ring and det-sp-reduction-compatibilities(2)-(3) directly; det-sp-unique-adjoint-coefficients is used only where the chosen adjoint changes. Step 10 applies det-sp-unique-right-adjoint with the letters exchanged; I checked the direction ε_G∘F(γ)=t. Step 12 normalization: lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement gives γ_{p_d}=Γ_{p_d}, so t is (1⊗I)∘PF^{-1}; the tower charts come from det-sp-tower-gluing(1),(3). Step 4: sk-lem-integral-models(2) characterizes condensed Dbc(X,O_E) as derived complete with constructible reductions, matching def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed (uniform bounds by dévissage); the Noetherian hypothesis of det-sp-normalized-equivalence holds. Step 7: the rational Hom chain via det-sp-rational-localized-hom is correct; naturality for h/ℓ^s follows by E-linearity. Statement: the added opening paragraph only makes the unit's def-pur-conventions setting explicit (k=F̄_q, ℓ≠p, finite A killed by a power of ℓ, and the named category equivalences); it adds no hypothesis and keeps the source text verbatim. The ℓ=p counterexample is correct. Edge cases checked: d=0/étale, empty X or Y, K=0, A=Z/ℓ², E=Q_ℓ, ramified E, three-field towers.
